description: Single three-dimensional surface plot (a calculated response surface with overlaid literature data points) showing the calculated improvement in yield strength, Δσ_P [MPa], produced by carbide precipitation in Fe–Mn–C–Al steel, plotted against two variables: carbide size [nm] (left horizontal axis, ticks 0-100 in steps of 20) and f, the volume fraction (right horizontal axis, ticks 0.0-1.0 in steps of 0.2). The vertical axis is Δσ_P [MPa] with labelled gridlines from 0 to 900 in steps of 100. The surface is drawn with a rainbow colour map — purple/blue (low) at large carbide size and small f, rising through green/yellow to red and dark red at the highest corner, i.e. small size combined with f approaching 1.0. Seven cube markers with vertical stems sit on the low-f edge of the surface, each labelled with a carbide and a reference: TiC [19], V(C, N) [19] (two markers), VC [21], V4C3 [20], VC/Fe3C [5] and NbC [19]. All markers lie between the 100 and 400 MPa gridlines; NbC lies at the largest carbide size (near the 100 nm end of the axis) and at the lowest Δσ_P, while TiC and VC sit at the smallest sizes. The figure demonstrates that increasing volume fraction and decreasing carbide size both raise the calculated precipitation strengthening.

subfigures.description: 3D coloured response surface of calculated yield-strength improvement Δσ_P [MPa] versus carbide size [nm] (0-100) and volume fraction f (0.0-1.0), with seven labelled cubic markers (TiC [19], V(C, N) [19] ×2, VC [21], V4C3 [20], VC/Fe3C [5], NbC [19]) plotted on stems at low f.

observations.observation: The plot is a 3D surface with vertical axis labelled Δσ_P [MPa], gridlines printed from 0 to 900 in steps of 100.
The two horizontal axes are labelled 'Carbide size [nm]' (ticks 0-100, step 20) and 'f' (ticks 0.0-1.0, step 0.2).
The coloured surface rises steeply to its highest, dark-red corner where carbide size is smallest and f is largest, and is lowest (purple/blue) at large carbide size and small f.
Seven cube markers with vertical stems are labelled on the surface: TiC [19], V(C, N) [19] appearing twice, VC [21], V4C3 [20], VC/Fe3C [5] and NbC [19].
All labelled markers lie between the 100 and 400 MPa gridlines of Δσ_P, i.e. in the low-Δσ_P region relative to the surface maximum near 900 MPa.
The NbC [19] marker is positioned at the largest carbide size (near the 100 nm end of the axis) and at the lowest Δσ_P of all plotted markers.
The TiC [19] and VC [21] markers lie at the smallest carbide sizes shown, at the far left corner of the plotted volume.

The caption states the figure is the calculated relation between the yield strength improvement with the volume fraction and size of carbide size in Fe–Mn–C–Al steel, adapted with permission, Copyright 2021, MDPI.
The citing text states M is the Taylor factor (3.06 for face-centred cubic metals), and G and b are the shear modulus.

The citing text states that higher volume fraction and smaller precipitate size, including Ti, V and Nb containing carbides, give obvious improvement in yield strength, supporting carbides acting as obstacles to dislocation sliding during plastic deformation.
The citing text states that κ carbides were reported to be sheared by Orowan bowing of dislocations, indicating they cannot offer continuous strengthening after yielding.
